title: The night my flight disappeared
text:
My flight to Warsaw was supposed to leave at nine, but the board kept changing its mind. First it was delayed by thirty minutes, then by two hours, and eventually the word "cancelled" appeared in red letters. Around me, people sighed, checked their phones, and formed a long queue at the airline desk.

I could have joined them, but I remembered a tip from a colleague who travels constantly: when everyone queues, go online. I opened the airline's app, found the rebooking option, and chose a morning flight within a minute. Then I used the chat on the website to ask about a hotel voucher. The agent replied politely, and ten minutes later I had a confirmation email.

The compensation was another story. The rules say you can claim money back if the delay was the airline's fault, but you need to keep every receipt and write a formal complaint. I did it from the hotel room, attaching boarding passes and screenshots.

Three weeks later, the money arrived. I will not pretend the night was pleasant, yet it taught me that patience is overrated. Calm, quick action usually solves more than standing in line and hoping for the best.
